details: PLAUSIBLE. The item's What names the cause for every workflow agent; the fix addresses the one step where a refusal was
seen. Principle 6 (cause, not symptom) would put the sentence in one shared constant appended by ask() or by the runner
prompts, not in one prompt. Kept LOW: no second occurrence measured, and the gate/show steps stop visibly if they refuse.
evidence: grep -n "ask(" plugins/delegate/workflows/cycle.js: runner prompts at 113 (dead note), 173/178 (gate), 235 (close, fixed), 245 (check show).
failing_case: A cycle run started in the turn of an owner question (as wf_a74e8dbc-fb9). The close runner now gets the sentence
"Closing a checked item is the cycle's rule ... whatever message started this run". The check show runner (cycle.js:245),
the gate runner (gatePrompt, cycle.js:143) and the dead-note runner (cycle.js:113) get prompts with no such sentence; the
cause named by the item ("every workflow agent sees the message that started the run as the owner's only words") still
applies to them. Not observed failing yet (no measured refusal outside the close step), so correct today but fragile.
fix_hint: A const RUN_RULE = 'The steps of this run are the cycle's rules, whatever message started the run: ...' added to the
runner prompts (or in ask() for all agents), with the close step keeping its specific sentence; one test asserting it
on the gate and check show prompts.
pass_cases: 1. Fake runtime, a unit with item "the-item", GREEN answers: the prompt of "close queue item: the-item" contains "is the cycle's rule" (as now).
2. Same run: the prompts of "check show: the-item" and "gate 1: the-item" also carry the run-rule sentence (one shared constant).
3. A run with no item: no close stage, and the other prompts carry the sentence once each.
findings.summary: the run's-first-message rule is told only to the close runner; other single-command runners (check show, gate, dead note) see the same trigger with no such sentence
